title: Lifecycle Logger
description: Write a script that logs every MonoBehaviour event method call, then observe the order in the Console.
problemStatement:
**Goal:** Deepen understanding of execution order.

1. Create a script `LifecycleLogger`.
2. Add `Debug.Log` inside these methods (even if empty): `Awake()`, `OnEnable()`, `Start()`, `Update()`, `FixedUpdate()`, `LateUpdate()`, `OnDisable()`, `OnDestroy()`.
   - For `Update`, `FixedUpdate`, `LateUpdate`, log only the first 3 frames to avoid flooding the console. Use a counter.
3. Attach the script to an empty GameObject.
4. Run the scene and observe the order of logs.
5. Stop, then in the Inspector disable and re-enable the GameObject while playing (or via script). Observe OnDisable/OnEnable calls.
6. Take a screenshot of the Console showing the initial sequence (Awake, OnEnable, Start, then first few Updates).

Briefly note the order you observed.
hints: Use a private int `frameCount` and increment in Update; log only if frameCount < 4.
OnDisable/OnDestroy: to test, you can create a UI button to toggle the object or simply stop Play mode.
expectedOutput: Console shows Awake → OnEnable → Start → (Update/FixedUpdate/LateUpdate repeats) → OnDisable (if toggled) → OnDestroy (when stopping).
